name: Kimodo SOMA RP v1.1
description: NVIDIA Kimodo trained on Bones Rigplay. Starts exactly from the current pose.

code.install: Set up the isolated motion worker in the ComfyUI_VNCCS_Utils folder: 'motion_worker/install.sh kimodo' then 'motion_worker/run.sh kimodo' (Windows: install.bat / run.bat; Docker: docker compose -f motion_worker/docker-compose.yml --profile kimodo up -d --build). See motion_worker/README.md.

requirements.notes: Most of the memory is the LLM2Vec text encoder. Set TEXT_ENCODER_DEVICE=cpu to keep it on the CPU; the motion model itself needs under 3 GB.

guide.summary: Starts exactly from the pose you made, with finger and spine detail (SOMA skeleton). Slower than ARDY, up to 10 s.
guide.best_for: Continuing your pose; walking, gestures, sports, everyday actions
guide.speed: Fast once loaded, slower than ARDY
guide.setup_effort: Medium: one command sets up an isolated worker

setup.label: Isolated motion worker
setup.detail: The model runs in its own venv next to this extension, so ComfyUI's packages are never changed and your other workflows keep running. In the custom_nodes/ComfyUI_VNCCS_Utils folder run the command once (it creates the venv), then keep the worker running next to ComfyUI. Windows (also ComfyUI portable): motion_worker\install.bat kimodo, then motion_worker\run.bat kimodo. No Python on the machine? Install uv first; the script then downloads Python 3.11 into the venv by itself. Optional, if you already use Docker: docker compose -f motion_worker/docker-compose.yml --profile kimodo up -d --build

setup.label: Text encoder (~16 GB)
setup.detail: Meta Llama 3 8B Instruct with the LLM2Vec adapters, downloaded into ComfyUI's models/text_to_motion/text_encoders folder (public copies of the original weights, no Hugging Face account needed; the Llama 3 Community License applies). The small Kimodo checkpoint is fetched on the first generation.
